title: doc2sequence
summary: Convert tokenized documents to embedding-vector sequences.

gpu_support.notes: `doc2sequence` consumes host tokenizedDocument and wordEmbedding objects and returns host cell/tensor outputs; it does not use provider kernels.

description: `doc2sequence(emb, documents)` returns a cell array whose i-th cell contains the embedding-vector sequence for the i-th tokenized document.
behaviors: `emb` must be a RunMat `wordEmbedding` compatibility object.
`documents` must be a RunMat `tokenizedDocument` compatibility object.
For embedding input, each output cell contains a D-by-S numeric matrix, where D is the embedding dimension and S is the sequence length.
Unknown words are discarded by default. Set `UnknownWord` to `"nan"` to include NaN vector columns for unknown words.
`PaddingDirection` accepts `"left"`, `"right"`, and `"none"`. The default is left padding.
`PaddingValue` accepts a finite numeric scalar and defaults to 0.
`Length` accepts `"longest"`, `"shortest"`, or a positive integer. Positive integer lengths truncate sequences on the right.
When `PaddingDirection` is `"none"`, output cells keep per-document sequence lengths, except that fixed or shortest `Length` values still truncate longer documents.
The `wordEncoding` input form is not implemented yet and remains tracked in the broader Text Analytics compatibility issue.
Very large padded dense outputs are rejected with a controlled error to avoid accidental memory explosions.

examples.output: `sequences` is a cell array of D-by-S matrices.
Each cell keeps the sequence length of the corresponding document.
Sequences are right-padded or right-truncated to length 100.

faqs.question: Does RunMat support `doc2sequence(enc, documents)` for `wordEncoding`?
faqs.answer: Not yet. This slice implements the `wordEmbedding` form; `wordEncoding` index sequences remain open work.

faqs.question: Does `doc2sequence` return single precision like MATLAB examples?
faqs.answer: RunMat numeric tensors currently use host f64 storage, so the compatibility output is numeric but not MATLAB's exact single-precision storage.

faqs.question: Does `doc2sequence` execute on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. It maps host text/object metadata to host cell and tensor outputs.

example.input:
sequences = doc2sequence(emb, documents)
sequences = doc2sequence(emb, documents, Name, Value)
example.output: `sequences` is a cell array of embedding-vector matrices.

points: `PaddingValue` must be a finite numeric scalar.
`Length` must be `"longest"`, `"shortest"`, or a positive integer.

gpu_residency: `doc2sequence` performs host text/object sequence construction and has no provider kernel.
